source.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ, τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: When then comes the Son of the Man in the glory of him and all the angels with him, then he will sit on throne of glory of him;

en.L: And when the Son of Man comes in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and all the angels with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sit on [the] throne of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory;
en.B: The Son of Man will come in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and all the angels with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat on the throne of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.
en.R: The Son of Man will come in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and all the angels will come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sit on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious throne.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in glory: Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Daniel one like a son of man comes before God and is given glory and a kingdom over all peoples. Jesus applies the picture to himself (24:30; 26:64).

decisions.choice: glory: the splendor and majesty of God's king
decisions.reason: The throne of his glory is the throne from which he rules and judges, as in 19:28.

decisions.choice: he will sit on the throne: the Son of Man is the judge
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as the one who judges all people (7:22-23; 16:27).

decisions.choice: his, him, he with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Unlike the figures in the parables before it, the Son of Man here is Jesus himself, so his pronouns take the usual span.

decisions.choice: glorious throne
decisions.reason: Readable uses the adjective, which keeps the key term.

source.text: καὶ συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων, καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων.

records.literal_gloss: And will be gathered before him all the nations, and he will separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, \v 33 and he will set the sheep on right of him, the but goats on left.

en.L: And all the nations will be gathered before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, \v 33 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set the sheep on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, but the goats on [the] left.
en.B: Every nation will be brought together before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will divide the people into two groups, the way a shepherd sorts the sheep from the goats. \v 33 He will stand the sheep at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand and the goats at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.
en.R: People from every nation will be gathered in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will separate them into two groups, like a shepherd who separates the sheep from the goats. \v 33 He will put the sheep on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right side and the goats on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.

decisions.choice: all the nations: all people of every nation
decisions.reason: "Them" in the next clause is masculine, so the people of the nations are meant, judged one by one. Whether Israel is included is debated; the scene seems to include all humanity.

decisions.choice: the shepherd separates sheep from goats: a daily task
alternatives: a picture of choosing better animals
decisions.reason: Sheep and goats grazed together in one flock and were separated, often at evening. The picture is of a simple sorting, not of the worth of the animals.

decisions.choice: right and left: the place of honor and its opposite
decisions.reason: To sit or stand at a ruler's right hand was the place of favor (Psalm 110:1).

decisions.choice: the people; into two groups
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is separated and how, following the meaning decision.

source.text: τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: Then will say the King to those on right of him: Come, the blessed of the Father of me, inherit the having been prepared for you kingdom from foundation of world.

en.L: Then the King will say to those on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, 'Come, you blessed of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from [the] foundation of [the] world.
en.B: Then the King will say to those at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, 'Come, you whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has blessed. The kingdom has been ready for you since the world was founded; now it is yours to inherit.
en.R: Then the King will say to the people on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, 'Come, you people {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has blessed! Receive the kingdom as your own. It has been ready and waiting for you since the world was made.

decisions.choice: the King: the Son of Man himself
decisions.reason: The King speaks of "my Father", so he is the Son of Man of 25:31, now named as king (compare 2:2; 27:11).

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as a gift that belongs to God's children
decisions.reason: An inheritance is not earned. The kingdom was prepared for them long before they acted.

decisions.choice: from the foundation of the world: from the beginning of creation
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 13:35. God's plan for his people was made before history began.

decisions.choice: King, with a capital
decisions.reason: The title belongs to the Son of Man himself, so it is capitalized, and his pronouns take the usual span.

decisions.choice: Receive the kingdom as your own
decisions.reason: Readable says what inheriting means without the legal word.

source.text: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με.

records.literal_gloss: I hungered for and you gave me to eat, I thirsted and you gave drink me, a stranger I was and you took in me, \v 36 naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, in prison I was and you came to me.

en.L: For I was hungry and you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [something] to eat, I was thirsty and you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} drink, I was a stranger and you took {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in, \v 36 naked and you clothed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I was sick and you visited {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I was in prison and you came to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.B: For when I was hungry, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} food; when I was thirsty, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a drink; when I was a stranger, you took {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into your home; \v 36 when I had no clothes, you dressed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; when I was sick, you looked after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; when I was in prison, you came to see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.R: When I was hungry, you fed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When I was thirsty, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water. When I was a stranger, you let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stay with you. \v 36 When I had no clothes, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} clothes to wear. When I was sick, you took care of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When I was in prison, you came to visit {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: a stranger: a traveler or foreigner far from home who needs a place to stay
decisions.reason: Hospitality to strangers was a duty the law commanded (Leviticus 19:34). To take in means to receive into one's home.

decisions.choice: naked: without enough clothing
decisions.reason: The word is used of someone poorly clothed as well as of someone with no clothes.

decisions.choice: visited: came to help and care for
decisions.reason: The verb means to look after someone in need.

decisions.choice: I was hungry: the King names himself in those who were in need
decisions.reason: The righteous are surprised by this (25:37-39), and the King explains it in 25:40.

decisions.choice: me with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The King is the Son of Man speaking of himself, so "me" takes the usual span.

source.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Then will answer him the righteous saying: Lord, when you did we see hungering and fed, or thirsting and gave drink?

en.L: Then the righteous will answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, 'Lord, when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry and feed [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}], or thirsty and give [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] drink?
en.B: Then the righteous will reply, 'Lord, when was it that we saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry and fed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, or thirsty and gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a drink?
en.R: Then the righteous people will answer, 'Lord, when did we ever see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry and give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} food? When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thirsty and give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} something to drink?

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who do what is right in God's eyes
decisions.reason: The word describes those on the King's right. Their surprise shows they did not act to earn a reward.

decisions.choice: when did we see you: a real question of surprise
decisions.reason: They did not know that they were serving the King.

decisions.choice: him, you with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: They speak to the King, the Son of Man, so "you" takes the usual span.

source.text: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν, ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν;

records.literal_gloss: When now you did we see a stranger and took in, or naked and clothed?

en.L: And when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a stranger and take [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] in, or naked and clothe [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}]?
en.B: When was it that we saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a stranger and welcomed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in, or without clothes and dressed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
en.R: When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as a stranger and invite {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} into our homes? When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} without clothes and give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} clothes to wear?

decisions.choice: the questions follow the King's list in order
decisions.reason: The righteous repeat each need the King named in 25:35-36.

source.text: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε;

records.literal_gloss: When now you did we see being sick or in prison and came to you?

en.L: And when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sick or in prison and come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'
en.B: When was it that we saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sick or in prison and came to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'
en.R: When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sick or in prison and come to visit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

decisions.choice: in prison: prisoners depended on visitors for food and care
decisions.reason: Prisons gave little food or care, so visits could mean survival.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ’ ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.

records.literal_gloss: And answering the King will say to them: Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did to one of these the brothers of me the least, to me you did.

en.L: And the King will answer and say to them, 'Truly I tell you, as much as you did [it] to one of the least of these {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you did [it] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.B: The King will answer them, 'Truly I tell you, each time you did it for one of these {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, even the least of them, you did it for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.R: And the King will answer, 'I tell you the truth, whenever you did these things for even the least important of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you were doing them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: the least of these my brothers: Jesus's followers in need
alternatives: anyone in need, believer or not
decisions.reason: Jesus calls his disciples his brothers (12:49-50; 28:10) and promises that whoever helps one of these little ones will be rewarded (10:40-42). Others read the words of every needy person, since the King names himself in all who suffer. The passage does not settle it.

decisions.choice: brothers: men and women alike
decisions.reason: The word in the plural often means brothers and sisters together (12:50).

decisions.choice: you did it to me: what is done to them is done to the King himself
alternatives: only counted as if it were done to him
decisions.reason: Jesus identifies himself with his brothers, as in 10:40: "Whoever welcomes you welcomes me."

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The word includes women, so the inclusive form is the default and the traditional form is the alternative.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 25:12, the solemn opening keeps the settled wording.

source.text: τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων· Πορεύεσθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Then he will say also to those on left: Depart from me those having been cursed into the fire the eternal the having been prepared for the devil and the angels of him.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say also to those on [the] left, 'Depart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to those at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left, 'Go away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who are under a curse, into the eternal fire that has been made ready for the devil and his angels.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to the people on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left, 'Go away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you people who are under a curse! Go into the eternal fire. It was made ready for the devil and his angels.

decisions.choice: depart from me: as in 7:23
decisions.reason: The King uses the words of 7:23, which echo Psalm 6:8.

decisions.choice: cursed, and a fire prepared for the devil: not prepared for them
alternatives: cursed by the Father, a fire made for people
decisions.reason: The blessed are blessed "of my Father" and the kingdom was prepared for them (25:34). Here neither is said: the curse is not called the Father's, and the fire was prepared for the devil and his angels.

decisions.choice: eternal: belonging to the age to come, without end
decisions.reason: The same word describes both the punishment and the life in 25:46.

decisions.choice: Depart (L); Go away (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:23, Literal keeps "depart" and Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: he, me with deity_pronoun spans; his angels with none
alternatives: a span on the devil's angels
decisions.reason: The King's pronouns take the span. "His angels" are the devil's.

source.text: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.

records.literal_gloss: I hungered for and not you gave me to eat, I thirsted and not you gave drink me, \v 43 a stranger I was and not you took in me, naked and not you clothed me, sick and in prison and not you visited me.

en.L: For I was hungry and you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [anything] to eat, I was thirsty and you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} drink, \v 43 I was a stranger and you did not take {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in, naked and you did not clothe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, sick and in prison and you did not visit {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.B: For when I was hungry, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no food; when I was thirsty, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} nothing to drink; \v 43 when I was a stranger, you did not take {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into your home; when I had no clothes, you did not dress {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; when I was sick and in prison, you did not look after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.R: When I was hungry, you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} food. When I was thirsty, you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water. \v 43 When I was a stranger, you did not let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stay with you. When I had no clothes, you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} clothes to wear. When I was sick and in prison, you did not come to take care of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: the list repeats 25:35-36 with each act left undone
decisions.reason: The judgment rests on what they failed to do. The last two needs are joined, shortening the list.

decisions.choice: the wording of 25:35-36, made negative
decisions.reason: Each level repeats its own wording of 25:35-36 so the two lists can be compared.

source.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;

records.literal_gloss: Then will answer also they saying: Lord, when you did we see hungering or thirsting or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and not did minister to you?

en.L: Then they also will answer, saying, 'Lord, when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'
en.B: Then they too will reply, 'Lord, when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry or thirsty, a stranger or without clothes, sick or in prison, and not come to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help?'
en.R: Then these people will answer, 'Lord, when did we ever see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or without clothes, or sick, or in prison, and not help {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

decisions.choice: serve: meet the needs of
decisions.reason: The verb is used of all kinds of care, from serving food to providing for someone (27:55).

decisions.choice: when did we see you: they too are surprised
alternatives: an excuse that they would have helped
decisions.reason: Like the righteous, they did not know the King was in those in need.

decisions.choice: come to your help
decisions.reason: Balanced says what serving meant here; Literal keeps "serve".

source.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ’ ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Then he will answer them saying: Truly I say to you, to the extent that not you did to one of these the least, neither to me you did.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will answer them, saying, 'Truly I tell you, as much as you did not do [it] to one of the least of these, you did not do [it] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} either.'
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reply, 'Truly I tell you, each time you failed to do it for one of these, even the least of them, you failed to do it for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.R: Then the King will answer, 'I tell you the truth, when you did not do these things for even the least important of these, you did not do them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: one of the least of these: the same people as in 25:40
decisions.reason: "My brothers" is not repeated, but the phrase points back to 25:40.

decisions.choice: nor to me: neglecting them is neglecting the King
decisions.reason: The King is identified with them in neglect as in kindness.

decisions.choice: the King
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: And will go away these into punishment eternal, the but righteous into life eternal.

en.L: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."
en.B: These will depart to eternal punishment, and the righteous will go to eternal life."
en.R: Then these people will go away to eternal punishment. But the righteous people will go to eternal life."

decisions.choice: eternal: belonging to the age to come, without end
decisions.reason: The same word describes the punishment and the life, setting them side by side (Daniel 12:2). Whether the punishment is conscious without end or a ruin that cannot be undone is not settled by this verse (compare 10:28).

decisions.choice: punishment: penalty given in judgment
decisions.reason: The word can mean correction, but here it is the judge's sentence.

decisions.choice: the end of Jesus's speech that began at 24:4
decisions.reason: The teaching on the Mount of Olives ends here; 26:1 returns to the story.
